# Copilot / automation guidance for setting up OpenEMR dev instance

## Purpose

This file contains explicit, repeatable instructions for Copilot and other automation agents to set up a working OpenEMR development instance (including initializing the MySQL database) so you do not need to re-prompt each time.

## High-level steps an agent should perform

1. Ensure prerequisites are installed:
   - PHP CLI (with required extensions for OpenEMR)
   - composer in PATH
   - Node.js + npm in PATH (if package.json exists)
   - MySQL reachable from the environment

2. Enable the installer and prepare the repository:
   - export OPENEMR_ENABLE_INSTALLER_AUTO=1
   - run composer install (if composer.json exists)
   - run npm ci (or npm install) and npm run build (if package.json and build script exist)

3. Run the automatic installer script with appropriate MySQL settings:
   - Use the included helper script if present:
     contrib/util/installScripts/auto_install.sh
     Example:
     ```bash
     OPENEMR_ENABLE_INSTALLER_AUTO=1 \
     MYSQL_HOST=localhost \
     MYSQL_PORT=3306 \
     MYSQL_ROOT_PASS="${{secrets.DB_ROOT_PASS}}" \
     MYSQL_USER=openemr \
     MYSQL_PASS="${{secrets.DB_PASS}}" \
     MYSQL_DB=openemr \
     contrib/util/installScripts/auto_install.sh
     ```

   - If not using the helper script, the equivalent manual commands are:
     ```bash
     export OPENEMR_ENABLE_INSTALLER_AUTO=1
     composer install --no-interaction --prefer-dist          # if composer.json exists
     npm ci --no-audit --no-fund || npm install --no-audit    # if package.json exists
     npm run build                                            # if package.json contains a "build" script
     php -d memory_limit=1024M -f contrib/util/installScripts/InstallerAuto.php \
       server=$MYSQL_HOST port=$MYSQL_PORT root=$MYSQL_ROOT_USER rootpass="$MYSQL_ROOT_PASS" \
       login=$MYSQL_USER pass="$MYSQL_PASS" dbname=$MYSQL_DB site=$SITE \
       iuser=$IUSER iuname="$IUNAME" iuserpass="$IUSERPASS" igroup="$IGROUP" \
       source_site_id="$SOURCE_SITE_ID" clone_database="$CLONE_DATABASE" \
       no_root_db_access="$NO_ROOT_DB_ACCESS" development_translations="$DEVELOPMENT_TRANSLATIONS" \
       loginhost="$LOGINHOST"
     ```

## Environment variables the agent should use (defaults shown)

- OPENEMR_ENABLE_INSTALLER_AUTO=1 (required)
- MYSQL_HOST=localhost
- MYSQL_PORT=3306
- MYSQL_ROOT_USER=root
- MYSQL_ROOT_PASS= (root password, if required)
- MYSQL_USER=openemr
- MYSQL_PASS=openemr
- MYSQL_DB=openemr
- SITE=default
- IUSER=admin
- IUNAME=Administrator
- IUSERPASS=pass
- IGROUP=Default
- SOURCE_SITE_ID= (for multisite cloning)
- CLONE_DATABASE= (set to "yes" or any non-empty value to clone DB)
- NO_ROOT_DB_ACCESS= (set non-empty when DB and user already exist)
- DEVELOPMENT_TRANSLATIONS= (set non-empty to fetch development translations)
- LOGINHOST=localhost

## Secrets handling (important)

- Never hardcode passwords in repo files or logs.
- For CI workflows (GitHub Actions, etc.) use repository secrets and mask them in logs.
- Avoid leaving credentials in shell history. Use ephemeral environment variables and CI secrets.

## Agent behavior notes

- Agents should check for the presence of composer.json and package.json and skip steps if missing.
- If root DB access is not available, set NO_ROOT_DB_ACCESS=1 and provide pre-created MYSQL_USER / MYSQL_PASS / MYSQL_DB.
- If using the helper script (contrib/util/installScripts/auto_install.sh), pass credentials via env vars instead of command-line args whenever possible. The helper still passes installer args on the PHP command line (InstallerAuto requires that), so ensure logs are scrubbed.

## Example GitHub Actions snippet (for maintainers who want CI)

Provide DB credentials as repository secrets (DB_ROOT_PASS, DB_USER_PASS, etc.), and run the helper script in a job that contains a MySQL service or uses an external test DB. Keep secrets masked.

## AI-generated code marking guidelines

Clearly mark code generated by GitHub Copilot or other AI assistants in this repository.

Add a comment at the beginning and end of the AI-generated section for code blocks.

Add a comment at the end of the line for single lines.

Include a note about AI generation for documentation or comments.

Be specific about which parts were AI-generated

Do not claim AI-generated code as entirely your own work

When making significant edits to AI-generated code, you may indicate the extent of modifications
